entries.title: Ezekiel 24:2
segments: Set himself against Jerusalem; by laying siege to it.  This was made known to the prophet n captivity by immediate revelation.  He writes the name of the day in the presence of the people, as a testimony to them when they shall hear of the event by human report.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:3
segments:
vv 3-5. 
 
  Set on a pot--seethe the bones; the pot is Jerusalem, the pieces in it are the inhabitants, and the fire under it is God's wrath.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:6
segments: Scum; rather, filth, adhering to the pot itself, as is plain

, polluting it and all in it. 
 
  Bring it out; the flesh.  This signifies the removal of the people from Jerusalem by death and captivity. 
 
  Let no lot fall upon it; lot to determine who shall be destroyed, and who saved: the meaning is, that all shall perish without distinction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:7
segments:
Her blood; the blood which she has shed. 
 
  Set it upon the top of a rock; shed it in the most open way. 
 
vv 7-8. 
 
God will make the punishment of bold transgressors as conspicuous as their crimes.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:8
segments: I have set her blood--not be covered; as she has shed blood openly, God will avenge it openly.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:9
segments:
vv 9-13. 
 
No amount of suffering inflicted upon transgressors is sufficient of itself to remove the desperate wickedness of the human heart.  Though God send upon them judgment after judgment, they will still continue to rebel against him.  The power of his Spirit alone can change the heart of stone to flesh and purify the inner man.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:10
segments: Spice it well; some prefer to render "stir it well."

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:11
segments: Then set it empty; after the pot is emptied of its contents, it is still further to be exposed to a fierce heat, that its filth may be molten out of it.  The meaning is, that after Jerusalem has been emptied of her inhabitants, the city itself is to be burned to the ground.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:13
segments: Purged thee; that is, assayed to purge thee.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:16
segments: The desire of thine eyes; the prophet's wife,

. 
 
God sometimes inflicts upon his most faithful servants great sufferings for the instruction of others.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:17
segments:
Tire; that is, turban.  This and the shoes were laid aside in mourning. 
 
  Lips; or beard, as the word is rendered in

.  This was covered as a sign of mourning. 
 
  The bread of men; of common men, that is, coarse bread, as in a time of mourning. 
 
vv 17-18. 
 
The interests of truth often require us to suppress those outward signs of grief which would be in other circumstances right and proper.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:21
segments: Pitieth; here in the sense of loveth with tenderness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:22
segments:
vv 22-23. 
 
  Shall not cover--shall not mourn; the calamity will be so general and overwhelming, that all the customary signs of mourning will be omitted.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:23
segments: Public calamity, long continued and general, has a tendency to harden the feelings of wicked men, so that they omit the customary expressions of grief and sympathy, and pine away in sullen despair.  From so dreadful a chastisement let every community seek deliverance from God by earnest prayer joined with hearty repentance.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:26
segments: To hear it; the desolation which I have made in Jerusalem: this expresses the certainty of the event in God's purpose.

entries.title: Ezekiel 24:27
segments: Be opened--be no more dumb; Ezekiel now closes, by divine direction, his prophecies to his own people till the capture of Jerusalem shall be reported to him,
.  His intervening prophecies were directed against the Gentiles.
